test_name: 2024 Reverse Stress Test (FSR November 2024, Chapter 2 Special Topic 1)
scenario_label: 13 banks designed bespoke scenarios to breach regulatory minimum capital within three years
capital_result: Scenarios were designed to breach regulatory minima; identified mitigating actions lifted capital above minima but well below prudential buffers.
other_results: Risk-weighted assets +27% on average from start to peak; net interest margin -60bp on average; largest losses driven by unemployment and property prices.
notes: Ranges are across participating banks. Residential and commercial property declines are start-to-trough changes in national indices.

test_name: 2020 COVID-19 Very Severe Scenario (benchmark cited in FSR November 2024, footnote 18)
scenario_label: Most severe RBNZ bank solvency stress test scenario to date
capital_result: Benchmark used to compare the 2024 reverse stress test; only the five largest banks participated.
other_results: Risk-weighted assets +28% on average. FSR text states residential and commercial property prices fell by 48 percent.
notes: The FSR states: unemployment peaked at 17.7 percent, annual GDP declined by 18 percent from start to trough, and residential and commercial property prices fell by 48 percent.

test_name: 2025 bank industry solvency stress test - scenarios (Reserve Bank Bulletin Vol. 88, No. 3)
scenario_label: Scenario 1: geopolitical shock and trade fragmentation; severe New Zealand recession
other_results: House prices decline to a mid-2016 nominal level; GDP falls for three years; OCR raised to 5.50% then cut rapidly; NZD/USD troughs at 0.48.
notes: Table 2 year paths: unemployment 5.2 (2025) to 10.5 (Year 2); house prices index 100 to 65; GDP growth -3.2% in Year 2.

test_name: 2025 bank industry solvency stress test - results (Reserve Bank Bulletin Vol. 88, No. 11)
loss_horizon: 4 years (aggregate loan loss rate, impairment expense over opening exposures)
capital_result: Aggregate CET1 fell from 13.2% (March 2025) to a low of 9.6% in Year 3 (-3.6pp; 4.5pp below base case); aggregate Total Capital Ratio low 12.3% (-4.3pp). Capital remained above regulatory minima (e.g. 9% TCR) but all banks moved into Stage 2 of the Capital Buffer Response Framework (distributions capped at 30% of earnings).
other_results: Impairment expense $0.2b in Year 0 to $5.5b in Year 1 (0.9% of opening assets); over $17b cumulative over four years; net interest income $13.4b to $11.6b; a further 10% fall in house prices raises mortgage impairments by 40%.
notes: Results before mitigating actions unless stated. Scenario 2 adds a severe retail deposit outflow and wholesale funding market closure over three months.

test_name: 2017 Financial Sector Assessment Program - Technical Note: Stress Testing the Banking Sector and Systemic Risk Analysis (IMF Country Report No. 17/119)
scenario_label: Adverse scenario: balance-sheet recession with sustained deflation and sharp real-estate correction
loss_horizon: Cumulative credit losses across credit books
capital_result: All banks would still meet minimum requirements, but most banks would breach their capital conservation buffer at the low point. Aggregate CET1 fell from 10.4% (June 2016) to 7.7% (2018), above the 4.5% minimum, then recovered to 10.5%.
other_results: Mortgage book average 1-year PD peaks at 2.2% in 2018 with loan-loss provision ratio 2.1%; real equity prices -30% by end-2018; private investment -12%; private consumption -3%.
notes: Scenario severity described by the IMF as exceeding the GFC: six quarters of negative growth peaking at -2.6% in 2017Q4 versus the GFC trough of -2.3% in 2009Q1.
